learningObjective: See why checkpoint memory contains both saved segment boundaries and temporary activations during recomputation, creating an optimum near the square root of depth.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG can align layer chains, saved versus discarded activations, recomputation segments, and the two memory terms. Mermaid cannot show the quantitative store-recompute geometry precisely.

pages.insight: The backpropagation slide shows why intermediate graph values are needed during reverse traversal.
The modeling slide explicitly describes gradient checkpointing as a memory-versus-computation tradeoff for samples that do not fit in memory.

deckReview.notes: The deck directly motivates both prerequisites: reverse traversal needs activations, and checkpointing deliberately recomputes them. It does not provide a reusable square-root tradeoff figure.
